questions.knowledge_point: Expressing the Limit of a Left Riemann Sum as a Definite Integral
questions.problem: Find the function $f(x)$ and the value of $b,$ given that ${\int }_{2}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=0}^{n-1}[{(2+\frac{5k}{n})}^{2}\cdot \frac{5}{n}].$
questions.worked_solution:
A definite integral can be defined as the limit of a left Riemann sum as follows:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{k})\cdot Δx
$$

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{k}=a+kΔx.$

Notice that we're given that the lower limit $a=2.$ 

Comparing the given summation with the general expression above, we see that $Δx=\frac{5}{n}.$ Therefore, 

$$
\frac{5}{n}=\frac{b-2}{n}\,⟹\,b=7.
$$

Consequently, ${x}_{k}=2+\frac{5k}{n}$ and $f({x}_{k})={x}_{k}^{2}.$

Hence,

$$
{\int }_{2}^{7}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=0}^{n-1}[{(2+\frac{5k}{n})}^{2}\cdot \frac{5}{n}].
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is $f(x)={x}^{2}$ and $b=7.$

questions.knowledge_point: Expressing a Definite Integral as the Limit of a Left Riemann Sum
questions.problem: What is ${\int }_{3}^{4}2{x}^{2}\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?
questions.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{3}^{4}2{x}^{2}\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=2{x}^{2},$ the lower bound is $a=3,$ and the upper bound is $b=4.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{4-3}{n}=\frac{1}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{4}2{x}^{2}\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(3+i\cdot \frac{1}{n})\,\cdot \frac{1}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(3+\frac{i}{n})\cdot \frac{1}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[2{(3+\frac{i}{n})}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: What is ${\int }_{0}^{3}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?
questions.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{3}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)={e}^{x},$ the lower bound is $a=0,$ and the upper bound is $b=3.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{3-0}{n}=\frac{3}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(0+i\cdot \frac{3}{n})\,\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[f(\frac{3i}{n})\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=0}^{n-1}[{e}^{3i/n}\cdot \frac{3}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Expressing a Definite Integral as the Limit of a Right Riemann Sum
questions.problem:
What is ${\int }_{2}^{8}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x+1)\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?

*Hint: Write down the missing expression in terms of $m$ and $n.$*

${\int }_{2}^{8}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x+1)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[\operatorname{ln}⁡($
{{field-1}}$)\cdot \frac{6}{n}]$
questions.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}f({x}_{m})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{m}=a+mΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{2}^{8}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x+1)\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x+1),$ the lower bound is $a=2$ and the upper bound is $b=8.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{8-2}{n}=\frac{6}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{8}\operatorname{ln}⁡(5x+1)\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}f({x}_{m})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[f(2+m\cdot \frac{6}{n})\cdot \frac{6}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[f(2+\frac{6m}{n})\cdot \frac{6}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[\operatorname{ln}⁡(5(2+\frac{6m}{n})+1)\cdot \frac{6}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[\operatorname{ln}⁡(11+\frac{30m}{n})\cdot \frac{6}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
